newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FTSE 100 trades dominate ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FTSE 100 trades dominate ahead of expiry.

text.p: FTSE 100 options were the focus of activity in the options market on Thursday ahead of tomorrow's expiry of November stock index options, traders said.

With a continued high level of open interest around the index's current levels and a heavy volume of "roll over" trades, dealers said it was difficult to predict which way the market would likely go in the wake of the expiry.
"If there is a bias I would say it is going to be negative after the expiry but it is very difficult to tell," said one options specialist.
"A lot of people are still in the 3900 puts, they will not want the index to go below 3900 and will be trying to prop the market up until the expiry."

Said another: "There is not a massive amount of directional trade, it is all volatility business and I know quite a lot of people have got different bets on...but I believe the index is being held up ahead of the expiry and will come off after."

Traders also noted a large out-of-the-money trade in December 3325 puts, but said this appeared to be designed to insure a large investment portfolio against a sharp market downturn in the wake of the UK budget on November 26.
"If I was a portfolio manager I might need to show I had some risk protection," the options specialist said.

Some trades were designed to cover positions after the sharp fall in the cash FTSE 100 index in the past month, traders said. The index dropped to an eight-week low of 3898.2 on November 7, some 4.5 percent below its record 4073.2 set October 21.
The index was down 3.1 points at 3,923.8 by 1621 GMT.
